title: PostgreSQL Migration Specialist
description:
Client Overview



Our client is an industry leader in cloud-native modernization, specializing in helping enterprises escape the high costs of legacy licensing. They excel at transforming Microsoft-stack workloads into optimized, open-source environments on AWS. By leveraging advanced automation and cloud-native tools, they eliminate technical debt and significantly reduce TCO (Total Cost of Ownership) for global organizations.



Job Overview



As a PostgreSQL Migration Specialist, you will be the technical anchor for the database transition layer. This role begins with an intensive 4–8 week initial project phase focused on the end-to-end migration of SQL Server environments to AWS-hosted PostgreSQL.



Key Responsibilities : 



Migration Execution: Lead SQL Server to PostgreSQL migration activities utilizing AWS Schema Conversion Tool (SCT) and AWS Database Migration Service (DMS).

Schema & Data Validation: Manage schema conversion, validate data integrity post-migration, and oversee migration validation activities.

Troubleshooting: Resolve complex migration bottlenecks and compatibility issues between source and target environments.

Cross-Functional Collaboration: Act as the bridge between the infrastructure and application layers, coordinating with PHP developers to resolve database compatibility issues.

Deployment: Assist with final migration execution and production cutover activities to ensure minimal downtime.

Required Skills

PostgreSQL Expertise: Strong background in PostgreSQL administration and development.

AWS Migration Tools: Hands-on, professional experience with AWS DMS and AWS SCT.

Migration Provenance: Direct experience supporting SQL Server to PostgreSQL migration paths.

Advanced SQL: Exceptional SQL skills with a focus on cross-platform compatibility.

Validation & Remediation: Expertise in PostgreSQL migration validation and high-level troubleshooting.



Nice-to-Have Skills : 



Application-Layer Support: Experience supporting database migrations at the application layer.

Stored Procedure Conversion: Familiarity with converting complex stored procedures and functions from T-SQL to PL/pgSQL.

AI-Assisted Engineering: Familiarity with AI coding assistants to accelerate stored procedure conversion and troubleshooting.

Soft Skills & Candidate Characteristics

Strategic Accuracy: A focus on data integrity and precise schema mapping to prevent downstream application failures.

Agility: The ability to pivot and troubleshoot during the high-pressure initial 4–8 week migration phase.

Collaborative Leadership: Strong communication skills to guide PHP developers on database-specific constraints and requirements.

Efficiency-Driven: A mindset focused on using AWS automation and modern AI tools to streamline the migration lifecycle.

Salary, Incentive and Benefits Packages





Competitive Salary

Comprehensive Healthcare: HMO coverage included.

Allowances: Training allowance, gym or food allowance.

Family Support: Educational assistance for dependents.

Growth & Security: Annual salary increases (as per contract) and a clear career path.

Engagement: Free food and drinks provided during virtual events and company trips.

title: Multilingual Voice AI Tester & Coordinator VA (iPad Required, Long-Term)
description:
Hi! I'm Diego, co-founder of Traduality. We make Fire Lingo — an iPad app that helps US credit unions (member-owned banks) talk with their members in the member's native language. The app uses AI to translate speech back and forth, and we're growing fast.



Every time we add a new language to Fire Lingo (Burmese, Vietnamese, Haitian Creole, Portuguese, and many more coming), someone needs to test it carefully before we roll it out to credit unions. That's where you come in.



This is a long-term contractor role. I'm looking for one VA to grow with us. We'll start light — one or two languages at a time, maybe 5–10 hours a week. As I build trust with you, we'll ramp up to at least 20 hours per week, ongoing, with the goal of you owning this whole process for us.



What you'll actually do



Find native speakers of a target language (we'll show you how) and schedule a 30-minute Microsoft Teams video call with them.



On the call, you'll role-play a banking conversation — you play the bank employee, they play the member — using the Fire Lingo iPad. You'll follow a script we provide that covers things like account balances, debit cards, loans, and so on.



Take notes when the AI gets something wrong and document what happened.



After the session, pull the conversation data from our admin panel and organize it in Excel / Word.



Hire a professional language reviewer (we have a network, you'll just need to coordinate) to evaluate the AI's output. Brief them, collect their report, and summarize it for our tech team in a simple format we'll give you.



Later in the process, run similar sessions with real credit union members in the United States to gather feedback.



We'll train you on everything. The SOP is already written.



Requirements — please read carefully before applying

- You must own an iPad from 2018 or newer. Fire Lingo runs on iPad. Without one, you cannot do this job. In your application, tell me the exact model and year of your iPad.

- Very clear, easy-to-understand spoken English. This is the most important one. You'll be speaking English into the iPad, and the AI listens to you to do its work. A strong accent will confuse the AI and ruin the test. Please send a 1–2 minute voice recording in English as part of your application. Applications without a voice recording will not be reviewed.

title: Social Media Manager — Multi-Client Agency (LinkedIn Focus)
description:
ClarityForge Studios is a small US-based media studio that produces podcasts, social media content, and editorial work for energy sector leaders, policy experts, and mission-driven organizations. We are looking for a sharp, organized, English-fluent Social Media Manager to take ownership of social content production and community engagement across our client portfolio.



This is a long-term contractor role. Our existing podcast production contractor started at 10 hours per week and has grown into a 40-hour-per-week position. We are looking for the same kind of growth here.



WHAT YOU WILL DO



Content Planning and Production (40%)

- Maintain weekly content calendars across LinkedIn, YouTube, X, Instagram, Threads, Bluesky, and Substack for each client

- Repurpose long-form content (podcasts, articles, transcripts) into platform-ready posts, threads, and short clips

- Write LinkedIn post copy in each client's voice using our master prompt library and AI tools, then refine until it sounds native

- Build short vertical clips with accurate captions and strong hooks (Descript, CapCut)

- Design simple graphics in Canva using brand templates we provide

- Apply our editorial filters to every piece of copy before it goes live



Scheduling and Publishing (15%)

- Schedule posts through Buffer across all client accounts

- Stagger times and vary hooks per our scheduling rules

- Coordinate cross-client publishing so nothing collides



Community Engagement and Multi-Account Management (30%)

This is the part of the role most social media VAs do not do well. We need someone who can do it carefully and sound like a real person on every account.

- Manage the Golden Hour (first 60-90 minutes after each post) using Buffer's Community tab

- Reply to incoming comments in the client's voice, referencing specific points to start real conversations. Generic responses like "Thanks for engaging" are not acceptable

- Run cross-account engagement through an anti-detect browser (GoLogin or AdsPower, set up by us)

- Vary timing and patterns to keep activity organic

- Monitor inbound comments, DMs, and mentions; surface anything needing direct attention

- Engage with target audiences by leaving substantive comments on relevant industry posts



Tracking and Reporting (15%)

- Update ClickUp with post status, assets, and due dates

- Track 2026 metrics that matter: comment depth, saves, post lifespan, target-title engagement (we do not track total likes)

- Produce a short weekly summary: what worked, what did not, what to test next week



WHAT WE ARE LOOKING FOR



Required:

- Native or near-native English writing. You will be writing copy that goes out under our clients' names. We will test this in the application.

- Strong copywriting instincts: short hooks, clean sentences, no filler, no clichés

- Experience using AI tools (Claude, ChatGPT) to draft and iterate on copy. You should know how to write a clear prompt and edit AI output until it sounds human

- Experience scheduling and managing multiple social accounts through Buffer, Hootsuite, or similar

- Familiarity with LinkedIn, YouTube, X, Instagram, Threads, and Substack basics

- Short-form video editing with captions (CapCut, Descript, or similar)

- Canva proficiency

- Reliable internet, quiet work setup, clear weekly availability



Nice to have:

- Prior experience managing a small ecosystem of related accounts (a founder profile plus a company page plus collaborators)

- Experience with anti-detect browsers (GoLogin, AdsPower, Multilogin)

- Interest in energy policy, science, or B2B media

- ClickUp experience



WHAT WE PROVIDE

- Documented operating plan and editorial filters that govern every post

- Master prompt libraries for AI-assisted copy in each client's voice

- Brand templates and visual assets in Canva

- Buffer and anti-detect browser tools, set up and paid by us

- Clear training, weekly check-ins, detailed feedback

- A team that values careful, thoughtful work over speed



HOURS AND PAY

- 10 to 20 hours per week to start

- $5 USD per hour, paid through Wise or similar

- Hours and rate review at 90 days based on performance and capacity. We grow people who do good work.

- Long-term contractor relationship. We are not looking for someone who will leave in three months.



HOW TO APPLY



Apply through OnlineJobs.ph with the following:



1. A short cover note (no template language) telling me why this role fits you

2. Your resume

3. Two examples of LinkedIn or social copy or social media clip you have created, with a one-sentence note on each explaining what the client was trying to accomplish

4. Your answer to this prompt:



Pretend a podcast guest left this comment under a client's LinkedIn post: "Great conversation. The point about permitting reform really stuck with me." Write a reply in the voice of the client (founder of a veteran-led energy initiative) that would start a real back-and-forth. Two to three sentences max.



Applications without the writing sample at the bottom will not be reviewed.

title: Part-Time Virtual Assistant — Social Media & Business Support
description:
I'm Andria Thurber — a life insurance broker, team builder, and founder of a growing personal brand called Come As You Are. My work sits at the intersection of protection planning, self discovery, conscious living, and community building. I'm looking for a part-time VA to grow with me.



This starts at 10 hours per week with room to expand as we grow together.

Starting rate is $3-4/hour based on experience, with opportunity for increases as the role expands.



The primary focus right now is social media. I'm active on
, Instagram, and LinkedIn. I have a strong, specific brand voice — and I need someone who can take what I give them and make sure it shows up consistently and beautifully. Right now, your primary job is to post and schedule the content I create. Over time, as you learn my voice deeply, there is opportunity to draft content for my review. I want someone who is excited about that growth.



I also want someone who uses AI tools confidently — whether that's for graphic creation, caption suggestions, scheduling optimization, or research. If you're not already using AI in your workflow, this probably isn't the right fit.



What you'll be doing:

Posting and scheduling content across
, Instagram, and LinkedIn. Creating simple graphics in Canva that match my brand aesthetic. Managing consistency so my presence stays active even during my busy weeks. Eventually — researching community outreach opportunities, finding venues for seminars and lunch and learns, and supporting organic lead generation in the community.



What I'm looking for:

Someone who is self directed and takes initiative. I give a task and I need you to go run with it — I'm not here to micromanage or coddle. Strong written English and communication skills. An eye for aesthetics and brand consistency. Someone who can study my existing content, understand my energy, and match my voice without being told twice. Organized, reliable, and honest about your capacity.



A little about how I work:

I'm direct and I move fast. I have high standards and I'll tell you when something isn't right — and I'll also tell you when you've done something great. I'm building something real and meaningful and I want someone who wants to grow alongside that, not just fill hours. As the role evolves, hours and compensation have the potential to increase.



To apply:

Please
 me with the subject line "I'm Your Person" — tell me in 3-5 sentences why you're the right fit, share links to any social media accounts or content you've managed, and answer this question: What does consistency mean to you when it comes to social media?



Applications that don't follow these instructions will not be considered.

title: Short-Form Video Editor
description:
Short-Form Video Editor (Premiere Pro + After Effects, or DaVinci Resolve), 

Full-Time Remote, UK Agency



About Us

We're a London-based creative content consultancy producing short-form 

social content for a small portfolio of growing brands. Tight team, fast 

pace, no bureaucracy. Strict NDA on client names.



The Role

You'll edit 10 to 20 short-form pieces per week in Premiere Pro with After 

Effects, or DaVinci Resolve with Fusion — your call, work in whichever you 

ship fastest in. Footage and assets are delivered to you via Frame.io and 

Google Drive. You cut, caption, motion-design, sound-design, colour, and 

export to spec. We review, you revise, we ship.



What you'll be editing (three repeating formats)



1) Podcast clips, talking-head with motion design

   60 to 90 second vertical cuts pulled from long-form podcast recordings. 

   Two-camera setup, separate audio tracks. Punchy hooks in the first 3 

   seconds, animated captions on-brand, lower thirds, light motion graphics 

   (kinetic type, callouts, simple transitions). Sometimes paired with a 

   matching square carousel for LinkedIn (5 to 8 slides in After Effects 

   or Resolve Fusion, exported as PNGs or 1x1 video).



2) Talking-head videos with supplied B-roll

   30 to 90 second vertical or square edits where we send you the A-roll 

   (presenter to camera) and a B-roll package. You cut the talking head 

   tightly, motivate B-roll insertions, add captions, light sound design, 

   colour-match A and B-roll. No need to source footage — it's all supplied.



3) Static and animated carousels (occasional)

   LinkedIn and Instagram square carousels built from supplied copy and 

   brand templates. 5 to 10 slides. Sometimes a short animated version for 

   the lead slide.



Weekly deliverables

- 10 to 20 short-form pieces, mostly 15 to 90 seconds

- Burned-in captions, brand-styled per client, accurate to audio

- B-roll cutaways motivated by content (not pasted on top)

- Light motion design (kinetic captions, callouts, lower thirds, end cards)

- Clean H.264 exports to platform spec (1080x1920, 1080x1080, 1920x1080)

- Organised project files returned to shared drive



Must have

- Fluent in either Premiere Pro + After Effects OR DaVinci Resolve + Fusion

- Strong captioning craft (kinetic, on-brand, accurate, not auto-generated 

  garbage)

- Portfolio of at least 5 short-form edits you personally cut, including 

  at least one podcast clip and one talking-head with B-roll

- Fluent written and conversational English

- Wired internet, minimum 50 Mbps down / 20 up

- Machine able to run your chosen software smoothly, minimum 16GB RAM, 

  dedicated GPU

- Daily 4-hour overlap with UK hours (3pm to 11pm Manila works)



Nice to have

- Real motion design chops (kinetic type, simple 2D animation in AE or Fusion)

- Carousel and static design (Photoshop, Illustrator, or Figma)

- Sound design and audio cleanup (iZotope RX, Fairlight, Audition)

- Real colour grading beyond auto-balance

- Familiarity with Frame.io, Notion, Slack



Pay

£500/month flat (approx PHP 35,000), paid via Wise on the 1st. 

60-day review for raise to £550 to £650 based on quality and ownership.

Paid trial task before hire: $40 USD flat on delivery.

13th-month bonus paid in December as standard.



Mon to Fri, 6 to 8 hours daily. Your weekends are yours.



How to apply

1. Start your
 with the word "PARSNIP" as the first line.

2. Send to 

   a) A 60-second Loom introducing yourself, showing your editing machine, 

      and explaining one decision you made on a recent edit and why.

   b) Links to 3 short-form edits you personally cut. At least one podcast 

      clip and one talking-head with B-roll. Tell me which one you're most 

      proud of and which one you'd redo.

   c) Screenshot of fast.com speed test and your software version numbers.

   d) Your monthly rate expectation.

   e) One sentence: "What's the most common mistake editors make on 

      the first 3 seconds of a short-form video?"

3. Subject line: PARSNIP, Short-Form Editor, [Your Name]



We respond within 5 working days to every application.

title: Podcast Research VA — List Building for Guest Pitching (No Outreach)
description:
The Role



I'm a 30+ year business owner who has been running a company with my husband, and I'm building a qualified list of podcast interview targets for myself as a solo guest. I need a research-only VA to find and qualify the right shows.



This is a defined project, not an ongoing role. The total scope is approximately 200–300 qualified podcasts over 8–12 weeks. If the work goes well and a second research phase becomes useful after my first round of pitches, I'd want to continue with the same person — but I'm not promising ongoing work, and I want to be upfront about that so you can d
 if the scope fits you.



This is research only. You will not write or send pitch
s, at least in this first round. Your job is to deliver clean, qualified podcast leads in a shared spreadsheet. I'll handle the outreach myself.



What I Speak About so you can recognize a fit when you see it, my niche covers:



- Couples in business together / husband-and-wife businesses

- Spouse of an entrepreneur (the supporting partner perspective)

- Long-term marriage paired with a long-term business (30+ year arc)

- "Marriedpreneur" / "couplepreneur" life/ "husband-wife business"/ "founders life"

- Adjacent: women in business who are married to entrepreneurs, faith-based women in business, family business / legacy



I pitch as a solo guest, not as a couple.



Deliverable

Approximately 200–300 qualified podcasts total, delivered in weekly batches of 20–30 into a shared Google Sheet (I'll provide the template). 



Each row contains:

- Podcast name

- Host name(s)

- Last episode date (confirmed from the feed)

- Recent guest count (out of the last 10 episodes)

- Audience signal (Apple ratings count, Listen Notes rank, or claimed downloads — whichever you can verify)

- Topic relevance (1 sentence — how my niche fits)

- Why this fits me (1 sentence)

- Best contact method 
 / website form / guest application page / social)

- Media-first score (1–5 — see screening section below)

- Source URL (Apple, Spotify, or host site)

- Notes



If you can't verify a data point, write "unverified" — do not guess.



Inclusion Criteria

A podcast qualifies only if ALL of these are true:



1. Topic relevance — host covers couples-in-business, spouse-of-entrepreneur, marriedpreneur life, OR is a women-in-business / faith-based business show whose audience would benefit from my angle.

2. Activity — new episode published within the last 60 days.

3. Format — interviews outside guests (not solo or co-hosts only).

4. Audience signal — at least one of: 100+ Apple Podcasts ratings, OR Listen Notes Global Rank under 10,000, OR 200+ downloads/episode per public claims.

5. Mid-tier preferred — Listen Notes rank roughly 2,000–50,000. Skip the very top of category charts; I already know those.



CRITICAL: Screening for Media-First Hosts

This is the most important part of the work. I want shows that are real media properties with engaged listeners — NOT shows that exist primarily as a marketing channel for the host's own paid course or coaching program. The latter rarely book outside guests with overlapping offers; the former are open and worth my time.



Use this screening framework for every candidate, in this order:



Where to look:



1. Podcast feed and recent episodes — is the show itself active and guest-driven?

2. Host website and bio — is the podcast presented as a standalone media property, or as a support channel for a paid offer?

3. Episode descriptions and guest patterns — do they regularly bring on outside guests rather than teaching solo?

4. Social profiles and pinned posts — does most promotion point to the show, or to their product?



Specific checks:

- Read the last 5–10 episode titles and note how many are guest interviews.

- Search the host's site for the course/program name and compare it to the podcast theme.

- Check whether the podcast has a separate landing page or just sits under the course brand.

- Scan social posts for the ratio of episode promotion to product promotion.

- Look for a free resources page, guest application, or media kit — this usually signals a broader media orientation.



Scoring (1–5):

- 5 — Pure media property. Almost all episodes are guest interviews. Podcast has its own landing page. Host clearly promotes the show as a show.

- 4 — Mostly media. Strong guest cadence; host has a product but it doesn't dominate the show's identity.

- 3 — Mixed. About half guests, half solo teaching. Worth pitching but expect more friction.

- 2 — Mostly course-funnel. Show is largely solo episodes selling the host's program. Skip unless the host's niche directly maps to mine.

- 1 — Pure funnel. Show exists only to promote the course. Do not include.



Include 4s and 5s. Mark 3s for my review. Exclude 1s and 2s unless I specifically tell you otherwise.



Sources to Draw From

- Listen Notes (search by keyword, sort by rank)

- Podchaser

- Apple Podcasts and Spotify category charts (Entrepreneurship, Marriage, Christianity & Spirituality, Self-Improvement)

- Guest histories of specific hosts I'll share with you (after the trial task)

- Feedspot directories for marriage / couplepreneur / women-in-business categories



Do not pad the list. Quality over quantity. If you can only find 18 qualified shows, deliver 18 — don't invent a 19th and 20th to hit the number. I will check.



Trial Task (Paid)



Before ongoing work, I run a paid trial:

- Pay: $35 flat 

- Task: Research 10 podcasts using the criteria above, delivered as a filled-in spreadsheet

- Turnaround: 48 hours from go-ahead

- What I'm evaluating: Quality of fit (did you read my niche correctly?), depth of research (did you find shows I likely don't know about?), and accuracy on the media-first score.



The strongest applicant is selected for the main project.



Project Scope, Timeline & Pay

This project has a deliberately staged structure because the size of this niche is genuinely uncertain — there may be 50 qualifying shows, there may be 200. We'll find out together.

- Discovery batch: First 30 qualified podcasts, delivered in 1–2 weeks. This batch tells both of us how deep the niche runs before committing to a larger scope.

- Continued research: Based on what the discovery batch reveals, I expect to commission additional batches of ~30 podcasts each, up to roughly 100 total, at the same rate. If the market is smaller than expected, we wrap earlier.

- Pay: $4 per qualified podcast

- Initial commitment: ~$120 for the discovery batch

- Realistic total range: $120–$400 depending on what the research reveals

- Quality clause: Pay applies to rows that pass spot-check. Rows with inaccurate data, padding, or that don't meet the criteria don't count toward the total. Be precise; don't pad.

- Payment schedule: Paid per batch within 48 hours of acceptance

- Communication: Brief weekly check-in 
/loom/zoom-15 min) during the project; async otherwise

- Future extension: If a later round of pitches generates good responses and I commission research into adjacent niches, I'd offer that work to the same person first.



Required Skills

- Excellent written English

- Spreadsheet fluency (Google Sheets)

- Strong attention to detail — I will spot-check 3–5 rows in every batch. Inaccurate, padded, or AI-hallucinated entries will end the engagement.

- Independent research capability

- Reliable on deadlines



Nice-to-Have

- Prior podcast research or podcast guesting experience

- Familiarity with Listen Notes, Podchaser, or Apple/Spotify podcast charts

- Any background in marriage, family, faith-based business, or women-in-business spaces



How to Apply

Reply with:

1. Prior podcast research experience (if any) — even one example helps.

2. One podcast you'd recommend I pitch and a one-sentence reason why. This is the most important part of your reply — I read it first. Please do not suggest the obvious top-charting shows.

3. Your time zone and weekly availability.



Generic AI-written replies that don't include a real podcast recommendation will be ignored.



Looking forward to working with the right person.

title: Operations Manager / Executive Assistant

Executive Assistant / Operations Right Hand



Location: Remote

The Opportunity



We are seeking a high-caliber Executive Assistant / Operations Right Hand to support the principal of a California-based real estate investment firm currently raising a development fund. The successful candidate will operate as a force multiplier, taking ownership of operational systems, financial and investing workflows, and stakeholder coordination while providing direct executive support to the principal.



This is not a traditional virtual assistant position. We are looking for people with prior experience as an Executive Partner at Athena, or as a Chief of Staff, Operations Lead, or senior EA at other agencies. Please indicate if you have had experience in one of these firms or your previous employer. 



Key Responsibilities



The role encompasses operational oversight of bookkeeping and financial workflows across multiple legal entities, working alongside an external bookkeeper to maintain accuracy and timeliness. It also includes supporting investor relations and capital activities, coordinating with property managers and contractors across the development portfolio, and helping improve operational processes over time. Additionally, the role will assist with ad-hoc project management and organization with managing the business. 



In addition to business operations, the role includes executive support functions such as calendar management, inbox triage, travel coordination, meeting preparation, and personal logistics. The successful candidate will serve as the primary point of contact for contractors, vendors, the bookkeeper, and legal counsel, managing follow-through so the principal is not pulled into day-to-day operational matters.



Communication is async-first, with daily check-ins in Pacific Time. Proactive identification and escalation of issues is expected.



Required Qualifications



Minimum two years supporting a CEO, founder, or executive directly in a right-hand capacity.

Demonstrated experience building or owning an end-to-end process or system. 

Comfort operating in ambiguous environments and exercising independent judgment. 

Excellent written English, given daily communication with US-based investors, legal counsel, and partners. 

Financial literacy sufficient to read a P&L and identify discrepancies. 

High reliability, accountability, and ownership mindset. 

Comfort managing senior stakeholders and direct reports.



Preferred Qualifications



Prior role as an Executive Partner at Athena is strongly preferred. Graduates of the Candidate Training Program are encouraged to apply and should reference this in their application.



Additional Considerations



EA or Chief of Staff background at Belay, Magic, Time, Wing, or comparable premium service providers. 

Experience in real estate, private equity, fund administration, or financial services. 

Familiarity with investor relations or fund operations. 

Prior experience managing direct reports.



Application Process



Qualified candidates should submit a brief summary of their most relevant prior role, with specific emphasis on direct support of a founder or executive. 

Candidates should also submit a two-to-three minute Loom video, unscripted, addressing the following prompt: "Describe a time you owned a process or system end-to-end. What did you build or improve, what was the resulting impact, and what would you approach differently today?" 

Please also include your available start date and desired role profile.



Applications without a Loom submission will not be considered. The Loom is the primary screening mechanism; written cover letters are not required.



Selection Criteria



This role prioritizes clarity of thought, communication, and independent judgment over formal credentials.



Candidates currently satisfied in their existing role should not apply. This position is intended for professionals seeking expanded ownership and the opportunity to operate across real estate operations and direct founder support.

title: Digital Artist / Illustrator
description:
Type: Contract / Freelance (project-based, with potential for ongoing work)



About the Role

We're looking for a digital artist/illustrator to create original artwork for printed collectibles. This is not a UI/UX role — we need someone who lives in illustration and graphic design, with a portfolio that shows range, polish, and an understanding of how artwork translates from screen to print.

Our preferred working style is iterative and collaborative. You'll be working closely with our creative directors — sharing rough concepts early, refining through rounds of feedback, and shaping the final piece together. We're looking for someone who treats creative direction as a partnership, not a handoff.



Responsibilities:

Produce original illustrations and graphic designs for printed collectibles

Work iteratively with creative directors — sharing thumbnails, sketches, and WIPs at each stage rather than presenting only finished work

Incorporate feedback quickly and constructively across multiple revision rounds

Deliver print-ready files that meet bleed, resolution, and color profile specs

Maintain consistency with established brand/character style guides

Collaborate with the production team to ensure artwork performs well on the target substrate (including holographic and specialty stock)



How We Work:

Concept phase: Share 2–3 rough thumbnails or directional sketches before committing to a final composition

Refinement phase: Iterate in stages (sketch ? lineart ? flats ? render), with check-ins at each milestone

Communication: Async via Slack/Figma/Notion with periodic live reviews; quick turnaround on revisions expected

Mindset: Open to creative direction, willing to push back with rationale when you have a stronger idea



Required Experience:

3+ years of professional illustration and/or graphic design work

Strong portfolio demonstrating original character/illustration work (not just layout or compositing)

Proven experience designing for print — not just digital/social

Demonstrated history of collaborating with art directors or creative leads through iterative review cycles

Solid grasp of color theory, composition, and typography



Required Tools:

Adobe Creative Suite — Photoshop and Illustrator (required); InDesign a plus

Procreate or equivalent for sketching/illustration

Figma, Frame.io, or Miro — for collaborative review and markup

Slack and Notion — for async communication and project tracking

AI models: Nano Banana, Image-gen-2, Flux, etc. 

Optional but valued: Affinity Designer/Photo, Clip Studio Paint, Blender (for 3D-assisted illustration)



Print Production Knowledge (Required):

Working knowledge of CMYK vs. RGB workflows and soft proofing

Understanding of bleed, safe zones, trim marks, and print resolution (300+ DPI)

Experience preparing files for commercial print runs

Familiarity with spot effects (foil, holographic, UV) is a strong plus



Deliverables:

Concept sketches and WIP files at each milestone

Layered source files (.PSD / .AI) with named, organized layers

Print-ready exports (PDF/X-1a or specified format) at correct resolution and color profile

Any custom brushes, swatches, or assets used



Nice to Have:

Experience designing trading cards, packaging, posters, or other collectibles

Background in pop culture, gaming, anime, or collectibles aesthetics

Comfort presenting work live and walking through creative choices



To Apply

Send your portfolio (link preferred), rate structure (hourly and/or per-piece), and 1–2 examples of print work where you can describe the creative direction process and how the piece evolved through feedback.

title: Webflow Developer
description:
About ProLegal:

ProLegal is a legal technology and services company dedicated to helping law firms grow and operate more effectively. One of our services, ProLegal Growth, provides law firms with complete branding and website solutions. We custom-built digital experiences designed to build trust, communicate clearly, and convert prospective clients.



We are now bringing our Webflow development capability fully in-house, and we are looking for a skilled Webflow Developer to be that dedicated resource.



About the Role:

This is a development and implementation role, not a design role. You will receive finished designs (brand guidelines, mockups, and creative direction) and your job is to build them accurately and professionally in Webflow.



You will be responsible for two core areas:

ProLegal's own website — ongoing updates, new pages, landing pages, and continuous optimization ProLegal Growth client sites — building and launching Webflow sites for law firm clients based on designs produced by our creative team



While Webflow development is the primary focus, there will also be opportunities to contribute to internal PHP-based systems and tooling as workload allows.



This is a long-term, full-time position with consistent work and direct collaboration with a small, senior team. All work goes through an internal review process before going live and you will not be expected to publish directly to production.



Responsibilities:



Build responsive, pixel-accurate Webflow sites from Figma or other design files

Manage Webflow CMS structure so clients and internal team members can update content without touching code

Maintain and update ProLegal's own website, including page edits, content updates, new landing pages, structural changes

Implement interactions and animations per design specifications

Write clean custom HTML/CSS (and basic JavaScript when needed) to extend Webflow's native capabilities

Ensure all builds are cross-browser compatible, mobile-responsive, and optimized for performance

Manage multiple projects simultaneously and communicate clearly on timelines and blockers

Participate in brief daily or weekly check-ins as needed with the team during US Pacific overlap hours



Requirements:

Two to three years of hands-on Webflow development experience with a portfolio of live, shipped projects

Demonstrated ability to take a finished design file and build it faithfully in Webflow — this is the core of the role

Expert knowledge of Webflow CMS, interactions, and custom code integration

Strong HTML and CSS skills; clean, purposeful code when native Webflow tools fall short

Solid understanding of responsive design across desktop, tablet, and mobile

Professional written and spoken English communication as you will be working directly with our US-based team

Ability to manage your own time and work independently in a remote environment

Available to overlap with US Pacific Time for at least 4 hours per day (between 8 a.m. and 3 p.m. PT, Monday–Friday)



Preferred but not Required:

Basic JavaScript for custom interactions or third-party integrations

Experience with Webflow client handoffs and setting up editor permissions

Experience with Figma — you need to be able to read design files and extract assets independently

Experience with PHP and MySQL. Our internal systems are PHP-based, and there may be opportunities to contribute to internal tooling and integrations beyond Webflow work

title: Tech Lead
description:
WeFlex exists to increase the life expectancy and quality of life for people with a disability, people in aged care, and Australian war veterans — through access to physical fitness, allied health, and therapy supports.



So far we've worked with over 3,000 Australians, partnered with over 2,300 Service Providers, and delivered over 50,000 sessions — giving our customers more than 36 years of additional life expectancy in aggregate.



We've grown 30x over the last 2.5 years and want to continue at a rate of 100% year on year.



The seat

You'll own WeFlex's full technology stack — Supabase, Airtable, n8n, GoHighLevel, Zendesk, Aircall, Wavix, Xero, plus our internal portals (Admin / Client / SP) — and the small high-output team that builds on it.



The role is deeply hands-on:



Solve problems Yvonne (COO) and James (CEO) bring you — translate ambiguous business problems into systems that work

Find the right tools for the job — strong opinions, but tool-agnostic in service of outcomes

Scope and build — write the spec, then build it (or hand to your team and run the sprint)

Project manage — run weekly sprints, ship reliably, surface blockers early

Adopt AI deeply — your workflow should be heavily AI-augmented (Claude / GPT / equivalent integrated into how you think and ship)

You'll inherit a tech team of ~5 builders and a roadmap that includes the O2C rebuild, Supabase migration, and live business-critical automation across our entire customer lifecycle.



What we're looking for

We hire skills over credentials.



Big AI adopter. You don't just use AI — your workflow runs through it. You can show us your stack and a real recent build where AI was core to how you executed.

Builder of systems. Real evidence of operational systems / automations / integrations you've shipped end-to-end. Portfolio matters more than CV.

Sprint-running project manager. You've run weekly or fortnightly sprints with a small team and shipped reliably.

Strong tool selector. You don't pick the tool you know — you pick the right tool. n8n, Make, Zapier, Python, Airtable, Supabase — you've used and chosen between them based on the problem.

Translates ambiguous problems into specs. When a COO hands you "clients aren't reporting back to us," you can diagnose, scope, and build — without needing the problem fully defined first.

Degree, years-of-experience, prior industry — all signals, not gates. If your work speaks, your CV doesn't have to be conventional.



What this role does NOT involve

Marketing tech / GHL funnel design

Direct customer service

Heavy DevOps / infrastructure architecture

Mobile / native app development 



Compensation

PHP 90,000–220,000 per month depending on experience and demonstrated capability

13th-month pay per Philippines labour law

6-month probation; 8-week mutual notice post-probation

Fully remote, AEST-aligned working hours (07:00–15:30 PHT typical)

This is a senior leadership seat reporting to the COO — peer to our Heads of Sales, CS, Marketing, and Service Providers

To apply

Submit your application here: 



The application has two parts:



Part 1 — Application form



Your CV

Portfolio link (GitHub, Loom library, case studies, live systems you've built)

3 short written answers

Notice period + salary expectation

We are a Germany-based e-commerce company selling household, cleaning, and personal care products across multiple European marketplaces. We’re looking for someone to fully own our marketplace operations day-to-day.

What You’ll Do

You’ll manage listings, content, compliance, and performance across TikTok Shop DE (our main channel), Amazon, Otto, Kaufland, eBay, and Temu. This covers product content, backend fields, imagery, compliance documents, advertising performance reviews, stock monitoring, weekly reporting, and supporting new product launches and marketplace expansion. You’ll also handle product image editing in Photoshop and use AI tools daily to move faster on copy, translations, and research.

What You Must Have

You need 3+ years of hands-on marketplace seller account experience, ideally across TikTok Shop DE, Amazon.de, Otto, and Kaufland. Strong written and spoken English is essential. Photoshop proficiency is required for product imagery. You must be confident and fluent with AI tools (Claude, ChatGPT) — this is how we work and you’ll use them every day. You should be a self-starter, detail-obsessed, and able to work independently. A Mac is preferred but not required.

Compensation & Schedule

$1,100 USD per month. Full-time, fully remote, with at least 4–5 hours daily overlap with German time (CET/CEST).
